user_prompt:
INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPT (rate the past week)
First assessment, Ms J (30), ward nurse, self-referred. C = clinician, P = patient.

P: I did one of those online tests and it said I've got severe OCD. So I thought I'd better get it checked.
C: What made you do the test?
P: After shifts I get these thoughts that I'm bringing germs home from the ward. To my partner. Which is silly, honestly, we've got proper infection control, it's really unlikely.
C: How much of the day do the thoughts take?
P: Forty-five minutes, maybe. Mostly in the evening.
C: How much do they bother you?
P: A bit. They're not too upsetting.
C: Do you try to push them away?
P: Most of the time, yes. And usually I can, I just put them aside.
C: Do you do anything because of them?
P: I wash my hands and arms a lot more than I need to at home. Altogether maybe another forty-five minutes a day.
C: Do you try not to?
P: Most of the time. Usually I can stop when I decide to.
C: What happens if you can't wash?
P: My partner turned the tap off once, as a joke. I felt tense and uncomfortable all evening.
C: Is there anywhere you avoid, or anything you don't do because of it?
P: No. Nothing.
C: How's work, and the rest of your life?
P: Fine. I do full shifts, I see my friends. It's a bit of a nuisance, nothing more.
C: Mood? Alcohol?
P: Fine. A glass of wine sometimes.
C: Any thoughts of harming yourself or anyone else?
P: No.

SYMPTOMS TO LABEL
S1: Thoughts that she might be carrying hospital germs home to her partner
S2: Extra washing of hands and forearms at home

Return the JSON object now.
